DrawId.description: An id for the new geometry, such as "base". It may not hold `|`, `,`, `~`, `#` or `]`, which a face name made from it would read as its own.

LengthExpr.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

Point2.description: A sketch point in mm: [x, y] or {"x", "y"}.

Point3.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

SketchTarget.description: The sketch: its feature id or its name (default: the one being edited).

anyOf.description: [x, y] where a coordinate may be an expression over the design's parameters, such as ["w / 2", 5]: a point that follows the parameters and is fixed; text naming no parameter, such as "5", is just that number, in the design's length unit (a JSON number is mm), and does not itself fix the point.
An existing point's id such as "l1.end" or "p3", or a snap such as "mid:l1".
A model vertex [x, y, z] in mm, projected into the sketch.
A point on a model edge [x, y, z] in mm, projected into the sketch.

SnapPoint.description: A sketch point: [x, y] in mm (a coordinate may be an expression), an existing point's id ("l1.end"), {ref} or {at}, a snap as text ("mid:<line>", "on:<curve>:x,y", "x:<a>+<b>:x,y", "vertex:x,y,z"), or a model {vertex} or {on_edge}.

input.description: Draw a circle from its centre and its radius or diameter.

center.description: The centre. A point's id or `{ref}` makes that point the centre, so the circle follows it.

connect.description:
Make a new point that lands exactly on an existing point (the origin too) coincident with
it. Default: true.

construction.description: Draw construction geometry, which is not part of a profile. Default: false.

diameter.description: The diameter, in mm, as `radius` is given. Used when `radius` is not.

id.description: An id for the circle. Default: one of the sketch's own.

radius.description:
The radius, in mm: a number, or an expression over the design's parameters, which makes
the radius a dimension driven by them. Wins over `diameter`. Give one of the two.

sketch.description: The sketch to draw in: its feature id or name. Default: the one being edited.

through.description:
A point the circle passes through, kept on it. With a placed centre and an existing
point, that point and `radius` both fix the radius.

input.title: CircleCenterParams

label: Center Diameter Circle

Created.description: What a command added to its sketch: the ids that the sketch has now and did not before.

constraints.description: Constraint ids, dimensions not among them.

wires.description: The ids of 3D curves, when the command made any.

output.description: What a drawing command returns for a line, a circle, an arc or a slot.

constraints.description:
The ids of the constraints added besides the curves' own: a coincident for a point that
landed on an existing one, a point on the curve for a point that was given by id, a radius
for a size given as an expression, what `infer` added.

created.description:
Everything the call added to the sketch: `{points, curves, constraints, dimensions}`, and
`wires` when there are any.

curves.description: The ids of the curves drawn, in order.

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

output.title: DrawResult

params: center: [x,y] or point ref (a coordinate may be an expression over the design's parameters: the centre is fixed and follows them; text naming no parameter, such as "5", is just that number, in the design's length unit (a JSON number is mm), and does not itself fix the centre), radius | diameter: number or expression (an expression naming a parameter is a dimension driven by it; with `through` a point ref, that and the point both fix the radius); through?: point ref (a point the circle passes through, kept on it: where the tool's second click snapped); construction?: bool; connect?: bool (default true: a new point landing exactly on an existing point, the origin too, is made coincident with it). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)
